articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Breaks Ground in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A site has been cleared for a $50 million EVO Entertainment destination in downtown Clearwater, Florida, signaling continued large-scale investment in multi-attraction FEC concepts. EVO Entertainment is known for combining bowling, cinema, gaming, and food and beverage under one roof. This development is a strong indicator of investor confidence in the experiential entertainment sector.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Set to Open in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: What is being billed as Texas' largest family entertainment center is slated to open in Houston in 2026, representing a major new competitive venue in one of the country's biggest metro markets. The project underscores the continued trend of large-format FECs expanding in high-population Sun Belt cities. FEC operators in the region should take note of the scale and attraction mix as a benchmark for the evolving market.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Fuels Attractions Boom Across the UAE
articles.summary: The UAE is experiencing a surge in indoor entertainment investment, with major IP-driven and experiential concepts driving significant footfall growth across the region. This boom reflects global demand for climate-controlled, year-round family entertainment destinations. FEC operators and investors can look to the UAE as a bellwether for large-scale indoor entertainment trends.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how artificial intelligence and guest data are reshaping ticketing, in-park purchasing, and the broader guest journey for attractions operators. The company's vision extends well beyond ticketing into a fully frictionless guest experience ecosystem. FEC operators should pay close attention as these tools become increasingly accessible and competitive differentiators.

articles.title: Robobike Brings Immersive Motorbike Racing Simulators to Entertainment Venues
articles.summary: UK-based Robobike has developed a multi-axis motion simulator attraction that combines physical riding sensations, haptic feedback, and connected competitive leaderboards for leisure and entertainment venues. The system is designed to sit between a traditional arcade experience and competitive social entertainment, making it a strong candidate for FEC attraction lineups. Its cross-venue leaderboard feature adds a layer of engagement that could drive repeat visits.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Its Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Game Concept
articles.summary: Jora Vision is broadening its range of competitive socializing attractions, a category that continues to see strong demand in FECs and entertainment venues worldwide. The company's focus on skill-based, socially engaging experiences aligns well with current consumer preferences for interactive group entertainment. FEC operators evaluating new attraction investments should track Jora Vision's expanding portfolio.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Grows in Summer 2026 but Rising Costs Squeeze Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement sector saw notable attendance growth in summer 2026, but operators are facing mounting pressure from rising operational costs that are eroding profit margins. The dynamic mirrors challenges faced by FEC operators globally as inflation and labor costs remain elevated. Understanding how international markets navigate this tension may offer useful lessons for domestic FEC operators.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Calls for GST Reform to Boost Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries (IAAPI) is pressing the government for GST rationalization to reduce the tax burden on amusement and entertainment venues. The association argues that current tax structures are suppressing consumer demand and hindering industry expansion. This development is relevant for FEC suppliers and investors with exposure to or interest in the fast-growing Indian market.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111: Frictionless Guest Experiences Take Center Stage
articles.summary: InPark's latest issue focuses on how technology is being used to remove friction from the guest journey across ticketing, in-park purchasing, and attraction design. Contributors include accesso, Jora Vision, and Alterface, giving FEC operators a broad look at the tools reshaping the guest experience. This issue serves as a practical industry resource for operators looking to modernize their venues.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center to Bring Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is opening a new multi-attraction venue on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, combining arcade games and a trampoline park. The opening adds to a wave of new FEC activity across the Southeast United States. Operators in adjacent markets should monitor the Launch brand's expansion footprint as it continues to grow.

articles.title: Sky Zone Among Seven New Tenants Opening at Popular Chicago-Area Mall
articles.summary: Sky Zone is set to open at a popular north suburban Chicago mall alongside major retail tenants including Toys 'R' Us and IKEA, underscoring the continued appeal of trampoline park brands as mall anchor tenants. This reinforces the trend of entertainment concepts filling space vacated by traditional retail. FEC operators and developers should note that mall landlords are actively seeking experiential tenants.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large-scale entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, highlighting the ongoing attrition facing legacy FEC venues that have not kept pace with evolving consumer expectations. The closure serves as a cautionary tale for operators who delay reinvestment in their attraction mix and guest experience. Understanding what drove the closure can help other FEC operators identify vulnerability in their own businesses.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Cuts Hollywood Bowl Target on Summer Heatwave Footfall Impact
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has lowered its price target for Hollywood Bowl Group after a summer heatwave reduced indoor footfall at the UK bowling and entertainment operator's venues. The analyst note is a reminder that weather patterns can materially affect FEC attendance even for indoor venues, particularly in markets without robust air conditioning infrastructure. FEC operators and investors should factor climate variability into their seasonal forecasting models.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror with The Conjuring: Beyond Fear
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are collaborating on a premium interactive horror experience called The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, raising the bar for Halloween programming at large-scale entertainment venues. The investment signals that operators are moving beyond traditional haunted attractions toward licensed, immersive, and ticketed premium experiences. FEC operators with Halloween programming should evaluate how premium tiering can boost revenue during the fall season.

articles.title: Six Flags Darien Lake Drops Fright Fest in Favor of All-Ages Halloween Events
articles.summary: Six Flags Darien Lake has discontinued its Fright Fest haunted event for 2026, replacing it with expanded family-friendly Halloween programming including Kids Boo Fest and additional Oktoberfest weekends. The strategic shift reflects a broader industry conversation about audience segmentation and whether scare-focused events serve a venue's long-term brand and revenue goals. FEC operators planning fall programming should consider how their Halloween offerings balance family and adult audiences.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Create AI-Powered Surf Park Technology Ecosystem
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a partnership combining advanced wave technology with AI-powered computer vision to deliver a more connected and personalized experience for surf park operators and guests. The integration allows real-time session analytics and personalized wave programming, setting a new benchmark for technology-driven guest experience in active entertainment venues. FEC operators with surf or active attractions should monitor how AI-driven personalization is raising the bar for the category.

articles.title: Gateway Ticketing Helps Hersheypark Handle Peak-Season E-Commerce Surge
articles.summary: Gateway Ticketing Systems supported Hersheypark in managing a major spike in online ticket demand by migrating a portion of e-commerce traffic to its new Galaxy web store during a high-volume promotional period. The real-world stress test allowed the park to validate the new platform's scalability before a full migration. FEC operators running aggressive promotional campaigns should evaluate whether their ticketing infrastructure can handle sudden demand spikes.

articles.title: The Back Nine Naperville Expands Indoor Golf Offering This Fall
articles.summary: The Back Nine in Naperville, Illinois is launching a new indoor fairway experience this fall, adding to the growing competitive socializing and indoor golf segment. Indoor golf concepts have proven to be strong revenue generators with high per-capita spend and broad demographic appeal. FEC operators looking to diversify their attraction mix should take note of this category's continued growth.

articles.title: Fresno's Former Bed Bath & Beyond Space Gets New FEC Tenant
articles.summary: A vacant Bed Bath & Beyond location in Fresno, California is being converted into a family entertainment concept, continuing the national trend of FECs backfilling big-box retail space. This kind of adaptive reuse offers operators relatively low-cost entry into established retail trade areas with built-in foot traffic. Developers and FEC operators should continue monitoring the pipeline of available big-box retail space as an expansion opportunity.

articles.title: Why Audio Design Should Be Built Into FEC Attractions From Day One
articles.summary: London-based Factory Immersive makes the case that audio is one of the most underutilized tools in attraction design, arguing it should be integrated from the initial concept phase rather than added as a finishing layer. Responsive, interactive audio systems can meaningfully shape atmosphere, guide guest behavior, and deepen emotional engagement. FEC operators investing in immersive or themed experiences should evaluate how their audio strategy supports the overall guest journey.

articles.title: Play Town Indoor Amusement Proposed for New Milford, Connecticut Site
articles.summary: A new indoor amusement concept called Play Town is being proposed for a site in Milford, Connecticut, adding to a wave of new FEC development across the Northeast. The project is currently in the planning phase and represents ongoing investor interest in the indoor family entertainment category. Local operators in the Connecticut market should monitor the proposal's progress.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opening in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center is set to open in Rock Springs, Wyoming, bringing dedicated FEC amenities to a smaller market that has seen limited investment in the category. The opening reflects the broadening geographic reach of FEC development beyond major metro areas. Operators and suppliers targeting secondary and tertiary markets should note continued demand for family entertainment options in these communities.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Interactive Themed Experience Design
articles.summary: Alterface, a leading developer of interactive dark ride and shooting gallery experiences, is marking 25 years in the themed entertainment industry with a retrospective on its design philosophy and technology evolution. The company's work spans numerous major theme park and FEC installations worldwide, making its insights relevant for operators evaluating interactive attraction investments. FEC operators considering interactive dark rides or shooting experiences should explore Alterface's portfolio as a benchmark.

articles.title: GTI China Expo 2026 to Focus on Smart Innovation and Digital-Physical Integration
articles.summary: The 18th GTI China Expo will take place September 10-12 in Guangzhou under the theme 'Smart Innovation, Global Connectivity,' spotlighting how digital technology is transforming the amusement and cultural tourism sectors. The event is a key sourcing and networking platform for FEC operators and suppliers looking to identify emerging game and attraction technologies from Chinese manufacturers. Operators planning capital purchases or new attraction installations should consider attending or monitoring product announcements from the show.

articles.title: Kaiqi Group: Three Decades of FEC and Play Environment Design
articles.summary: China-based Kaiqi Group has grown from a playground equipment manufacturer into a comprehensive FEC design and manufacturing partner, with installations in over 120 countries across theme parks, FECs, and mixed-use developments. The company's operations-first philosophy integrates master planning, IP theming, engineering, and operational support into a single service offering. FEC operators seeking turnkey play environment solutions should be aware of Kaiqi as a major global supplier.

articles.title: InPark Editor: Let the Guest Experience Lead Technology Decisions
articles.summary: InPark Magazine publisher Martin Palicki argues that the goal of frictionless technology should always be to serve the experience, not to showcase the technology itself, drawing on examples from accesso's ticketing work and Jora Vision's attraction design. The editorial is a useful framing piece for FEC operators evaluating technology investments and vendor pitches. Operators who keep guest experience as the north star are better positioned to make technology choices that actually move the needle on satisfaction and spend.

articles.title: Practical Guide to Getting Started on Sustainability for Attraction Operators
articles.summary: A new perspective piece argues that sustainability in the attractions industry does not require perfection, but rather a practical, incremental approach that allows operators to act without being paralyzed by the scale of the challenge. The author acknowledges the resource constraints most FEC operators face and offers a framework for making decisions that move in the right direction. As sustainability becomes an increasingly important factor for guests and investors, FEC operators should begin building a roadmap even if the path is not fully clear.
